# Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } }, src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:1:import { getCurrentUser, listUsers } from "@/lib/users";

content.text:
I used **Postmark** for the welcome and password reset emails, and both are wired into `src/lib/users.ts`. Postmark only does transactional email, delivers reliably, and handles bounces and spam complaints for you. Its official Node SDK has no runtime dependencies.

The build and lint pass. I tested both flows with a fake Postmark API in place of the real one, and everything below worked. Nothing has been sent through a real Postmark account yet.

**What happens now**
- **New user:** `createUser()` adds the user and sends the welcome email. `users.ts` had no way to create a user before, so I added it.
- **Password reset:** `requestPasswordReset(email)` emails a one-time link that expires after 60 minutes. `resetPassword(token, newPassword)` sets the new password.
  - The response is the same whether or not the email has an account, so it can't be used to check which addresses are registered.
  - Each link works once. Using one cancels the user's other links.
- **If an email fails, nothing else breaks.** The error is logged and the signup or reset request still goes through. In testing, a signup still succeeded when Postmark refused the email.
- Passwords are stored hashed and never come back from the user functions.

**Files**
- `src/lib/postmark.ts`: connects to Postmark. It only connects when an email is actually sent, so the app builds without the token set.
- `src/lib/email/index.ts`: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`.
- `src/lib/email/templates.ts`: the wording and layout of both emails, in HTML and plain text. They live in code, so you don't need to set up templates in the Postmark dashboard.
- `src/app/forgot-password` and `src/app/reset-password`: two small pages so the emailed link opens a real page.
- `.env.example`: placeholders for `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN`, `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL`, `POSTMARK_MESSAGE_STREAM` and `APP_URL`. I added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because its existing `.env*` rule would have kept this file out of git.
- Added the `postmark` and `server-only` packages.

**Before it can send real email**
- Put a real Postmark server token in `.env.local`.
- `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL` must be an address or domain you've verified in Postmark.
- Users and reset links are kept in memory, like the existing users code, so they're lost when the server restarts. Move them to the database when Notely gets one.

`npx tsc --noEmit` on its own fails with an error in the existing `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found). It only depends on types that `next build` generates, and the build passes. I haven't committed anything.
